items.title: Have you head of bot-sitting?
items.summary: Botsitting is the work of checking and fixing what AI hands you. One Founder Reports survey asked people who use AI weekly and have trained a new employee. 40% said AI took less effort than training someone, so it may still save time for some people. But the checking still counts as work. If your job is turning into review, I think it's worth tracking where your hours go. Has AI made you faster, or has your work just changed shape?

items.title: AI Could Make Great Healthcare Affordable for All
items.summary: In episode 1045 of the SuperDataScience podcast, Jon Krohn discusses with Ben Hein, CEO at Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, how artificial intelligence has the potential to make high-quality healthcare universally accessible and affordable for everyone. Ben explains that AI will significantly enhance physician productivity, particularly in areas like diagnosis and detection through advanced pattern recognition. This transformation promises a future where excellent medical care is no longer a luxury but a global standard.

items.title: Can an AI Model Retrain Itself? Meta Just Tried It
items.summary: Sign up for updates on our NEW AI engineering book: https://www.louisbouchard.ai/book/?utm_source=yt-lf&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=book Meta's Self-Improving Memory research, explained for AI engineers. A model (Kimi K2.6) rewrites the prompts that manage its own agent memory and keeps the versions that score best (harness optimization). Then the same model is fine-tuned with LoRA on its own best runs (harness distillation). You'll see how the LOAD and OFFLOAD memory prompts work, why the best memory design (running summary, RAG, skill library or hypothesis tracking) changes with the task, how a meta agent rewrites its own instructions after reading its failures, what the retrained model keeps, and three things you can reuse in your own agents today without retraining anything. items.title: Chimps Quit When Paid (Michael Tomasello)
items.summary: Chimpanzees quit the moment they're paid. Children keep working until their partner gets paid too. Michael Tomasello, developmental psychologist at Duke University, on experiments comparing chimpanzees and human children in collaboration, and why shared agency is what makes humans different. The full conversation with Michael Tomasello is out on Machine Learning Street Talk on 24 November. #Shorts #MichaelTomasello #Chimpanzees #Cooperation #Cognition #MLST

items.title: Deriv Open-Sourced Its Staff AI Platform After 221 Skills Became a Permissions Mess
items.summary: Deriv's AI team open-sourced a platform that lets 900 staff build and share AI agent skills with enterprise access controls, security reviews and guardrails.
